title: Nineteen Hours and One Late Bell
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：day　|　正文 346 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 day 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 the caretaker ① kept a day that no clerk in the office would have logged, and he said the keeping was the whole of the duty. The ② day, meaning the daylight and not the working day, ran nineteen hours and stayed unrecorded on the sheet; a day, he said, is the only thing in a building that is judged by how long it is left unwritten.

Every ③ day in that building had the same late bell against it, and the ④ day at the end, meaning the one they kept for the stocktaking and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever counted twice. A day, his deputy said, is nine parts waiting and one part somebody willing to keep; the caretaker said the keeping is the part that fills nineteen hours.

The manager meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the day was the whole of the contract, meaning the working day and not the daylight. The ⑥ day, meaning the working day and not any of that, is the only thing in a contract that everybody signs for and nobody finishes; day, she said, is either something you keep or the only word that means both a daylight and a working day. She said the working day is the part they remember.

By 1961 the ⑦ day had become a line in a rota, and the rota had become an argument about the late bell. The ⑧ day of the whole thing, the caretaker wrote in August, was one building and nineteen hours of keeping; day, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to keep. She said the keeping was never mentioned.

The ⑨ day I remember is the one at the end, which was logged in 1974 and is still described as the longest in the building. A ⑩ day, the deputy said in 1976, is the only thing that improves by being kept; every day, she said, is a working day that has agreed to look like a daylight. She said the working day was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 一天；一日（指那栋楼里度过的那一天）
B. n. 白天；日光（指那段天光本身，与那个工作日相对）
C. 固定搭配：keep a day 值守一天
D. n. 一天（指留给盘点用的那一天）
E. n. 日子；白昼（抽象总称，指一栋楼里的全部值守）
F. n. 一天（指排班表上写到、被排定的那一天）
G. n. 工作日（指合同里约定的工作时长单位）
H. n. 工作日（抽象总称，指人人签字却无人做完的那一段）

items.q: kept a day that no clerk in the office would have logged
The day, meaning the daylight and not the working day
the day was the whole of the contract
The day, meaning the working day
the day had become a line in a rota
The day of the whole thing
A day, the deputy said in 1976

answers.why: keep a day 意为“值守一天”，1953 年管理员值守了一天办公室里没有一位职员肯登记的一天。
day 意为“白天、日光”，指那段天光本身而不是那个工作日，它延续了十九个小时而未记在表上。
day 意为“一天”，指那栋楼里度过的每一天，每一天都对着同一声迟到的铃。
day 意为“一天”，指留给盘点用的那一天，是唯一有人计算过两次的。
day 意为“工作日”，指合同里约定的工作时长单位，经理说这个工作日就是那份合同的全部。
day 意为“工作日”，指人人签字却无人做完的那一段而不是那段天光，是合同里人人都签字、却无人做完的东西。
day 意为“一天”，指排班表上写到、被排定的那一天，到 1961 年这一天成了排班表里的一行。
day 意为“日子、白昼”，管理员八月写道，整件事的值守是一栋楼和十九个小时的守候。
day 意为“一天”，我记得的是末尾那一天，1974 年被登记，至今仍被说成楼里最长的一天。
day 为抽象总称，副手 1976 年说，一天是唯一会因为被好好值守而变得更好的东西。
